content.content: {"sections": [{"spans": [{"text": "It\u2019s probaby the most wholesome Hollywood story ever.", "modifiers": {"bold": true}}], "indent": 0, "quoted": false, "type": "plain", "is_rtl": false}, {"spans": [{"text": "Charles Bronson worked on a show with a very young Kurt Russell, then a ten-year-old child actor. Russell knew it was his older co-stars birthday, and he admired him so he decided to buy him a birthday gift \u2014 a small remote controlled airplane. Bronson took the gift, opened it, and walked off the set without saying a word.", "modifiers": {}}], "indent": 0, "quoted": false, "type": "plain", "is_rtl": false}, {"spans": [{"text": "", "modifiers": {"image": "https://qph.cf2.quoracdn.net/main-qimg-a38c6f63b782bb4d08cde77df0ecfb15", "height": 707, "width": 687, "master_url": "https://qph.cf2.quoracdn.net/main-qimg-2ed1d8064b7dcec6aa62d5bc2281c36a", "is_deleted": false, "is_sensitive": false, "is_uploaded_by_bot": false, "zoomable": true, "dominant_color": "#9b999c", "has_transparency": false, "desktop_crop": {"x": 0, "y": 8, "width": 687, "height": 549}}}], "indent": 0, "quoted": false, "type": "image", "is_rtl": false}, {"spans": [{"text": "Russell was afraid he\u2019d upset a man he idolized by giving him a \u201cchildish\u201d gift \u2014 Bronson came across rather serious, stoic and stern. But a short while later, he was called to Brosnon\u2019s dressing room and found the actor visibly emotional. Bronson explained he had grown up dirt poor with fourteen siblings and had never, ever, received a birthday gift before in his entire life. A little model airplane that could actually fly would have been his dream gift, had he been a child.", "modifiers": {}}], "indent": 0, "quoted": false, "type": "plain", "is_rtl": false}, {"spans": [{"text": "This is why Bronson had to walk out; he needed to get himself together, collect himself. Because he didn\u2019t want everyone on the set to see him break down. Kurt Russell recalls how Bronson later gifted him a skateboard for his own birthday and the two of them would ride skateboards together between sets, as Bronson was unexpectedly good at skateboarding.", "modifiers": {"bold": true}}], "indent": 0, "quoted": false, "type": "plain", "is_rtl": false}]}

{"sections": [{"spans": [{"text": "", "modifiers": {"image": "https://qph.cf2.quoracdn.net/main-qimg-b81b04a4d697e5211e86073f4592d832", "height": 535, "width": 932, "master_url": "https://qph.cf2.quoracdn.net/main-qimg-f04557b22d91ae617c09b867dfbddd77", "is_deleted": false, "is_sensitive": false, "is_uploaded_by_bot": false, "zoomable": true, "dominant_color": "#212020", "has_transparency": false}}], "indent": 0, "quoted": false, "type": "image", "is_rtl": false}, {"spans": [{"text": "In July 2015, Richard Berry, the mayor of Albuquerque, was driving back to City Hall from lunch when he saw a man on a street corner holding a cardboard sign. It read, “Want a Job. Anything Helps.” Berry went to his staff and said the city should take that man at his word.", "modifiers": {}}], "indent": 0, "quoted": false, "type": "plain", "is_rtl": false}, {"spans": [{"text": "By September, the city had pulled an old Dodge van from its motor pool, put new tires on it, and wrapped it with the words There’s a Better Way. St. Martin’s Hospitality Center, Albuquerque’s largest homeless shelter, ran the program. Two mornings a week, a driver named Will Cole took the van to the street corners where people were asking for money.", "modifiers": {}}], "indent": 0, "quoted": false, "type": "plain", "is_rtl": false}, {"spans": [{"text": "On one windy March morning in 2016, people stood outside St. Martin’s waiting for Cole and his van. At each stop he got out and fist-bumped everyone who climbed in. He told them “good morning, ma’am” or “sir,” and he loaded their bags into the back himself.", "modifiers": {}}], "indent": 0, "quoted": false, "type": "plain", "is_rtl": false}, {"spans": [{"text": "One man he stopped for was Fidel, who said he was from Cuba. Cole asked if he wanted to work that day. Then he told Fidel he looked cold. Fidel said he had slept in the street the night before. Cole asked if that was every night, and Fidel said yes. Fidel got in the van.", "modifiers": {}}], "indent": 0, "quoted": false, "type": "plain", "is_rtl": false}, {"spans": [{"text": "The crews picked up litter and pulled weeds for the city’s Solid Waste Management Department. The shift lasted five hours. Workers got breakfast and lunch, and at lunchtime staff from city behavioral health departments came out to talk with them. Each person was paid $9 an hour in cash, which came to $45. The state minimum wage was $7.50. Berry said it was hard work, with shovels and rakes in the hot sun. A worker named John told PBS the job gave him “a sense of accomplishment,” and he wished it ran more days. Cole said that if he owned a business, he would hire many of these people in a second.", "modifiers": {}}], "indent": 0, "quoted": false, "type": "plain", "is_rtl": false}, {"spans": [{"text": "At the end of the day, the van took everyone back to St. Martin’s. Staff there helped with housing, job searches and health care. Kellie Tillerson of St. Martin’s said many workers had not known those services existed. One man who had just left prison came back the next day. St. Martin’s signed him up for its day labor program, told him about behavioral health services, and began helping him get an ID.", "modifiers": {}}], "indent": 0, "quoted": false, "type": "plain", "is_rtl": false}, {"spans": [{"text": "After three years, the city counted 6,666 one-day jobs held by 1,575 workers. Seventy-six of them had found permanent work. Seattle started a program modeled on Albuquerque’s. The city ended the original program in 2020, and a new version called Better Way Forward began in 2024.", "modifiers": {}}], "indent": 0, "quoted": false, "type": "plain", "is_rtl": false}, {"spans": [{"text": "In May 2016, KRQE rode along on one of the van’s mornings. Thomas Trusley, 68, said he had been a shop mechanic until a layoff left him homeless a year and a half earlier. His first goal was permanent work. With that day’s pay, he planned to buy shaving gear and cologne so he would look presentable. He had no jacket, but he had a clean shirt, and he called it his “Sunday dos.”", "modifiers": {}}], "indent": 0, "quoted": false, "type": "plain", "is_rtl": false}, {"spans": [{"text": "", "modifiers": {"image": "https://qph.cf2.quoracdn.net/main-qimg-632f7e4c278b3ad86b06dd42167112c7", "height": 413, "width": 720, "master_url": "https://qph.cf2.quoracdn.net/main-qimg-59bfc151481b7d8bb1a8217d6b0fe5ab", "is_deleted": false, "is_sensitive": false, "is_uploaded_by_bot": false, "zoomable": true, "dominant_color": "#9fab97", "has_transparency": false}}], "indent": 0, "quoted": false, "type": "image", "is_rtl": false}]}

It was January 28, 2014. Steve Davis, the charge nurse in the neuro intensive care unit at Trinity Medical Center, had texted him a picture of a CT scan. It showed a bleed in the brain of a patient named Tony Robinson. By Hrynkiw’s reading, the man had a 90 percent chance of dying without an operation. Hrynkiw was Trinity’s only brain surgeon.", "modifiers": {}}], "indent": 0, "quoted": false, "type": "plain", "is_rtl": false}, {"spans": [{"text": "Snow and ice had covered the city while he was in the operating room. Trinity tried to find someone to drive him, but the roads were blocked, even for emergency crews. He told Davis he would leave the car and walk.", "modifiers": {}}], "indent": 0, "quoted": false, "type": "plain", "is_rtl": false}, {"spans": [{"text": "It was about 20 degrees. He had a coat over his scrubs and the slip-on shoes from the operating room. “It’s not going to happen on my shift,” he said of the patient’s death.", "modifiers": {}}], "indent": 0, "quoted": false, "type": "plain", "is_rtl": false}, {"spans": [{"text": "He slipped and slid, and at one point he rolled down a hill. He got up and kept going. As he walked, he checked the patient’s vitals by text and asked the team to get the man and the operating room ready. At the bottom of the mountain he sat in a stuck ambulance for a few minutes to warm up. Along the way he stopped to help strangers push their cars out of a ditch.", "modifiers": {}}], "indent": 0, "quoted": false, "type": "plain", "is_rtl": false}, {"spans": [{"text": "At Trinity, the cell signal kept fading. Davis said that at one point he heard Hrynkiw say he was walking. Hours went by. Davis told the authorities, and the police went looking, but nobody found him.", "modifiers": {}}], "indent": 0, "quoted": false, "type": "plain", "is_rtl": false}, {"spans": [{"text": "About a mile from Trinity, a sales rep gave Hrynkiw a ride the rest of the way. ...", "modifiers": {}}], "indent": 0, "quoted": false, "type": "plain", "is_rtl": false}]}

contentQtextDocument.legacyJson: {"sections": [{"spans": [{"text": "", "modifiers": {"image": "https://qph.cf2.quoracdn.net/main-qimg-90c088ae3b7ae9c58bc16670d274c39a", "height": 405, "width": 720, "master_url": "https://qph.cf2.quoracdn.net/main-qimg-6e28f82a80c993e81c5b185ebf79f6ac", "is_deleted": false, "is_sensitive": false, "is_uploaded_by_bot": false, "zoomable": true, "dominant_color": "#51525d", "has_transparency": false}}], "indent": 0, "quoted": false, "type": "image", "is_rtl": false}, {"spans": [{"text": "In the summer of 1995, Adam DeVine, who was 11, left a store in Omaha, Nebraska, with his friends. They had gone for candy. A friend across the street shouted for him to hurry, and Adam heard “the coast is clear.” He walked his bike into the road, and a cement truck hit him. He went under its first two wheels and slid about 500 feet.", "modifiers": {}}], "indent": 0, "quoted": false, "type": "plain", "is_rtl": false}, {"spans": [{"text": "“They say the reason I lived was the bike took the hit first,” he said years later. He woke up two weeks later in intensive care, after doctors had kept him in a medically induced coma. He had broken everything from the waist down except his right femur, and his legs were crushed below the knees. His ribs were broken and his lungs were punctured. Doctors came close to amputating his legs and did not know if he would walk again.", "modifiers": {}}], "indent": 0, "quoted": false, "type": "plain", "is_rtl": false}, {"spans": [{"text": "At first he had to learn to lift his head off the bed, and then to sit up. Standing hurt. One day he started to cry and wanted to give up. His physical therapist smacked him in the face and yelled, “Yes, you can! Never say no! Never give up!” That hit got him to focus on his recovery. He had 26 surgeries over more than two years, at Children’s Hospital & Medical Center in Omaha.", "modifiers": {}}], "indent": 0, "quoted": false, "type": "plain", "is_rtl": false}, {"spans": [{"text": "In his wheelchair, he called a local radio station and did impressions, including Chris Farley. Back at school, he used jokes to answer bullies. By eighth grade he could play football. He has said he still lives with pain from those injuries.", "modifiers": {}}], "indent": 0, "quoted": false, "type": "plain", "is_rtl": false}, {"spans": [{"text": "As an adult, Adam went back to that hospital. Our meetings took place in one of the meeting rooms at a local church that Karen and her family attended. Karen\u2019s mom, who was one of the Girl Scout leaders, was a beautiful, lovely lady. One evening, she invited a few of us girls into the sanctuary. As we stood near some lit candles, she told us how much Jesus loved us and that we should always try to stay close to Him. The reverent way she shared this had me in awe at such a tender age.", "modifiers": {}}], "indent": 0, "quoted": false, "type": "plain", "is_rtl": false}, {"spans": [{"text": "That lovely lady died a few years later of breast cancer. content.content: {"sections": [{"spans": [{"text": "I loved Patrick Stewart\u2019s 1999 take on \u201cA Christmas Carol\u201d.", "modifiers": {"bold": true}}], "indent": 0, "quoted": false, "type": "plain", "is_rtl": false}, {"spans": [{"text": "It was a made-for-TV flick and way more enjoyable and well-made than it had any right to be, being a direct-to-DVD production that never even graced the silver screen or premiered in a cinema. Of all Dickens adaptions for this particular tale, this is the finest by far, to me.", "modifiers": {}}], "indent": 0, "quoted": false, "type": "plain", "is_rtl": false}, {"spans": [{"text": "", "modifiers": {"image": "https://qph.cf2.quoracdn.net/main-qimg-6279c23f133f9dea1daf0bf416393cad", "height": 1976, "width": 3000, "master_url": "https://qph.cf2.quoracdn.net/main-qimg-bb8cf54882eb0e022f297c7ea1ba2631", "is_deleted": false, "is_sensitive": false, "is_uploaded_by_bot": false, "zoomable": true, "dominant_color": "#202626", "has_transparency": false}}], "indent": 0, "quoted": false, "type": "image", "is_rtl": false}, {"spans": [{"text": "Stewart\u2019s ", "modifiers": {}}, {"text": "Christmas Carol ", "modifiers": {"italic": true}}, {"text": "didn\u2019t invent anything, didn\u2019t reinvent the genre for a modern audience, didn\u2019t rewrite the dialogue or alter the plot. It was completely and utterly faithful to the source material, and I loved that. Because far too many films appear terrified of staying faithful\u2026 they change a bunch of stuff to \u201cfit the times better\u201d. This one stayed true to itself, stayed true to the story, and Stewart played Ebenezer Scrooge exactly as he was thought of by Dickens almost 200 years prior. That\u2019s real craftmanship and I loved every second of it.", "modifiers": {}}], "indent": 0, "quoted": false, "type": "plain", "is_rtl": false}, {"spans": [{"text": "A lot of people will rave about Picard, or Professor X, and Sir Patrick Stewart nailed those parts, I won\u2019t argue against that for one singular second! But his Ebenezer Scrooge was sublime and the finest ever portrayed on film, and he did it in an almost forgotten straight-to-TV flick almost 30 years ago.", "modifiers": {"bold": true}}], "indent": 0, "quoted": false, "type": "plain", "is_rtl": false}]}

content.content: {"sections": [{"spans": [{"text": "Apart from his performance as Jean-Luc Picard in Star Trek, I can talk about how much gravitas he brought as Professor X in ", "modifiers": {}}, {"text": "X-Men", "modifiers": {"italic": true}}, {"text": " franchise or his irreplaceable body of work as a Shakespearean thespian or his wacky sense of humour that compelled him to voice \u2018poop emoji\u2019 in the dumpster fire known as ", "modifiers": {}}, {"text": "The Emoji Movie", "modifiers": {"italic": true}}, {"text": " (2017).", "modifiers": {}}], "indent": 0, "quoted": false, "type": "plain", "is_rtl": false}, {"spans": [{"text": "But I won\u2019t. I\u2019ll remember him for the charities he supported and how he reconciled with his traumatic childhood.", "modifiers": {"bold": true}}], "indent": 0, "quoted": false, "type": "plain", "is_rtl": false}, {"spans": [{"text": "", "modifiers": {"image": "https://qph.cf2.quoracdn.net/main-qimg-4da453ac8aaf1f2c7abbf1018f5bdbc9", "height": 1920, "width": 1920, "master_url": "https://qph.cf2.quoracdn.net/main-qimg-2d308cbf6e6d9571f248f1c2c843ce1c", "is_deleted": false, "is_sensitive": false, "is_uploaded_by_bot": false, "zoomable": true, "dominant_color": "#453630", "has_transparency": false, "desktop_crop": {"x": 0, "y": 0, "width": 1920, "height": 1536}, "caption": "Patrick, age 1."}}], "indent": 0, "quoted": false, "type": "image", "is_rtl": false}, {"spans": [{"text": "Sir Patrick\u2019s father, Alfred, was a Regimental sergeant major during the Second World War who returned England after surviving Dunkirk whereas his mother, Gladys, worked as a weaver. She was the light of his life. He also had two elder brothers whom he loved dearly.", "modifiers": {}}], "indent": 0, "quoted": false, "type": "plain", "is_rtl": false}, {"spans": [{"text": "The family\u2019s patriarch had come home a changed man from the battlefield; Alfred was irritable and had a notoriously short temper. He would lash out at his wife and three sons over inconsequential matters. Corporal punishment became a staple in the house. Gladys was a frequent victim of domestic violence and Patrick felt guilty for not keeping her safe. The troubled home life made young Patrick an introvert.", "modifiers": {}}], "indent": 0, "quoted": false, "type": "plain", "is_rtl": false}, {"spans": [{"text": "His dominating father made him feel small. He had no interest in school or his future prospects. Had Patrick stayed on this path he would\u2019ve joined a generation of lost boys.", "modifiers": {}}], "indent": 0, "quoted": false, "type": "plain", "is_rtl": false}, {"spans": [{"text": "When he was twelve his English teacher Cecil Dormand handed out copies of Shakespeare\u2019s ", "modifiers": {}}, {"text": "The Merchant of Venice ", "modifiers": {"italic": true}}, {"text": "and forced Stewart to take part in the play. He obliged and was allowed for the first time in his life to feel enormous and \u2018seen\u2019 for a talent even he was unaware of. ", "modifiers": {}}, {"text": "That talent was performing arts. And that\u2019s how he got to know what he was supposed to do in his life.", "modifiers": {"bold": true}}], "indent": 0, "quoted": false, "type": "plain", "is_rtl": false}, {"spans": [{"text": "", "modifiers": {"image": "https://qph.cf2.quoracdn.net/main-qimg-ce75215634bd27af0a5b323ca4beb630", "height": 576, "width": 960, "master_url": "https://qph.cf2.quoracdn.net/main-qimg-990bb0db3c6acecad1c1d0eaf9880a41", "is_deleted": false, "is_sensitive": false, "is_uploaded_by_bot": false, "zoomable": true, "dominant_color": "#61625d", "has_transparency": false, "caption": "Patrick with his parents."}}], "indent": 0, "quoted": false, "type": "image", "is_rtl": false}, {"spans": [{"text": "He chose the stage, opted for drama classes and did odd jobs to afford his passion but he was always strapped for cash. Years later Sir Patrick discovered that Cecil was his silent benefactor who would cover any unpaid dues. In 2010 when Patrick Stewart got knighted, he invited Cecil to sit alongside him because he didn\u2019t forget his professor\u2019s kindness.", "modifiers": {}}], "indent": 0, "quoted": false, "type": "plain", "is_rtl": false}, {"spans": [{"text": "", "modifiers": {"image": "https://qph.cf2.quoracdn.net/main-qimg-6bacbfa37a4bd2dce0be5bd27d9a01b8", "height": 576, "width": 960, "master_url": "https://qph.cf2.quoracdn.net/main-qimg-0c2b85712282dc2a1d5bceba7114f7a2", "is_deleted": false, "is_sensitive": false, "is_uploaded_by_bot": false, "zoomable": true, "dominant_color": "#a1abd2", "has_transparency": false, "caption": "Stewart standing next to Dormand in 2004."}}], "indent": 0, "quoted": false, "type": "image", "is_rtl": false}, {"spans": [{"text": "He picked up the quality of helping people and showing generosity by supporting charities that sheltered women and children from abuse. He honoured his mother through philanthropy.", "modifiers": {}}], "indent": 0, "quoted": false, "type": "plain", "is_rtl": false}, {"spans": [{"text": "", "modifiers": {"image": "https://qph.cf2.quoracdn.net/main-qimg-b4b13bc94c82c8297234617a10b2442d", "height": 220, "width": 540, "master_url": "https://qph.cf2.quoracdn.net/main-qimg-40b8ac585f36bd4deae305795aa42dd6", "is_deleted": false, "is_sensitive": false, "is_uploaded_by_bot": false, "animated_url": "https://qph.cf2.quoracdn.net/main-qimg-40b8ac585f36bd4deae305795aa42dd6", "should_autoplay": true, "zoomable": true, "dominant_color": "#000000", "has_transparency": false, "desktop_crop": {"x": 96, "y": 0, "width": 391, "height": 220}, "mobile_crop": {"x": 96, "y": 0, "width": 391, "height": 220}}}], "indent": 0, "quoted": false, "type": "image", "is_rtl": false}, {"spans": [{"text": "But what about his father, the architect of his harsh early life?", "modifiers": {"bold": true}}], "indent": 0, "quoted": false, "type": "plain", "is_rtl": false}, {"spans": [{"text": "Stewart searched for rationale to understand Alfred\u2019s behaviour. He wanted to know how a man could be so cruel to his own flesh and blood? The answer was in front of Patrick all along: undiagnosed PTSD or shell shock as it was called back then. This condition didn\u2019t excuse Alfred\u2019s violence but it did explain why he was so aggravated once the war ended. So Patrick forgave his long-dead father. In the end, Sir Patrick chose to become a bigger man and began raising awareness for mental health. He established another charity that looked after traumatised veterans.", "modifiers": {}}], "indent": 0, "quoted": false, "type": "plain", "is_rtl": false}, {"spans": [{"text": "His life story reminds me of neglected children. All a child needs is a good person who\u2019s willing to help even when nobody\u2019s looking. It can be anyone, even you and I. ", "modifiers": {}}, {"text": "Be the one who gives another person a chance to discover their self worth.", "modifiers": {"bold": true}}], "indent": 0, "quoted": false, "type": "plain", "is_rtl": false}, {"spans": [{"text": "", "modifiers": {"image": "https://qph.cf2.quoracdn.net/main-qimg-8755f2a787164dc16d6f590daf03dd19", "height": 490, "width": 540, "master_url": "https://qph.cf2.quoracdn.net/main-qimg-f8e9de0c5044d1a932b29c937e815b1f", "is_deleted": false, "is_sensitive": false, "is_uploaded_by_bot": false, "animated_url": "https://qph.cf2.quoracdn.net/main-qimg-f8e9de0c5044d1a932b29c937e815b1f", "should_autoplay": true, "zoomable": true, "dominant_color": "#010102", "has_transparency": false, "desktop_crop": {"x": 0, "y": 0, "width": 540, "height": 432}, "caption": "Sir Patrick Hewes Stewart (1940-2026), aged 86."}}], "indent": 0, "quoted": false, "type": "image", "is_rtl": false}, {"spans": [{"text": "I would like to conclude this article with a quote by Sir Ian McKellen\u2019s Magneto:", "modifiers": {}}], "indent": 0, "quoted": false, "type": "plain", "is_rtl": false}, {"spans": [{"text": "Death comes for us all. It\u2019s all I know for sure. The question isn\u2019t \u2018are you prepared to die?\u2019", "modifiers": {"italic": true}}], "indent": 0, "quoted": true, "type": "plain", "is_rtl": false}, {"spans": [{"text": "The question is \u2018who will you be when you close your eyes?\u2019", "modifiers": {"italic": true}}], "indent": 0, "quoted": true, "type": "plain", "is_rtl": false}, {"spans": [{"text": "There\u2019s no superior legacy other than leaving the world in a better shape than it was the day you were born. Your life, your choices, and most importantly your actions have the potential to leave an impact.", "modifiers": {"bold": true}}], "indent": 0, "quoted": false, "type": "plain", "is_rtl": false}, {"spans": [{"text": "Thank you for reading.", "modifiers": {"bold": true}}], "indent": 0, "quoted": false, "type": "plain", "is_rtl": false}]}
